title: Towards a monolithic platform for coupling superconducting circuits to low-loss microwave phonons in AlScN on 4H-SiC
authors: Yuanchen Deng, William W. Roberts, Sueli Skinner-Ramos, Dalton Anderson, Katherine Hewey, Xingyu Du, Michael Miller, Brandon Smith, Hwijong Lee, Pingping Chen, Charles Thomas Harris, Roy H. Olsson, Lisa Hackett, Rupert Lewis, Matt Eichenfield
abstract: Hybrid superconducting-phonon quantum processing is promising for cavity QED, measurement-based quantum computing, and other quantum applications. Relative to microwave photons at the same frequency, phonons can provide ultra-compact footprints, extremely low losses, and greater connectivity. Phonons can also couple strongly to superconducting circuits through the piezoelectric effect. However, this promise rests on scalable platforms that achieve these benefits without degrading superconducting circuit performance. This motivates a monolithic platform combining low phononic loss, strong electromechanical coupling, and superconducting-circuit compatibility without requiring suspended phononics. Here, we characterize a monolithic quantum acoustic platform combining aluminum superconducting circuits on exposed silicon carbide (SiC) with piezoelectric aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN) on SiC for integrated phononics. This architecture is enabled by selective removal of AlScN from selected chip regions, allowing aluminum superconducting microwave resonators to be fabricated directly on the SiC while preserving adjacent AlScN-on-SiC regions for phonon transduction. The resulting Al-on-SiC resonators exhibit a coherent lifetime of 2.9 μs, demonstrating compatibility with aluminum superconducting quantum devices. In parallel, cryogenic surface acoustic delay-line measurements on the retained AlScN-on-SiC regions show low phononic propagation loss at 4.05 GHz, corresponding to an estimated phonon lifetime of 7.6 μs. Together with a previously demonstrated electromechanical coupling coefficient of about 4.3% and a theoretical upper bound of 8%, these results establish Al-on-SiC/AlScN-on-SiC as a promising monolithic platform for integrating superconducting microwave circuits with piezoelectric phononic components for quantum acoustic networking and hybrid quantum systems.
summary: The paper presents an experimental demonstration of a monolithic platform integrating superconducting microwave circuits with low-loss piezoelectric phonons using $	ext{AlScN}$ grown on $	ext{SiC}$. By selectively etching the material, they create a structure that supports both high-quality superconducting resonators and long-lived acoustic waveguides. This establishes a promising starting point for building complex quantum processors utilizing phonon mediation.
main_problem: The goal is to develop a scalable, monolithic platform that can efficiently couple superconducting microwave circuits with low-loss microwave phonons for quantum applications.
main_result: The authors demonstrated the feasibility of an Al-on-SiC/AlScN-on-SiC architecture, achieving measurable lifetimes ($	ext{T}_1 \approx 2.9 \mu	ext{s}$, phonon $	au \approx 7.6 \mu	ext{s}$) and a coupling coefficient ($ eta \approx 4.3\%$) suitable for hybrid quantum systems.
method: The methodology involves fabricating superconducting resonators directly on exposed SiC regions while preserving adjacent AlScN-on-SiC regions for phonon transduction, followed by cryogenic characterization of both components.
model_or_system: The physical system is a monolithic heterostructure combining aluminum superconducting circuits (CPW resonators) with piezoelectric Aluminum Scandium Nitride ($	ext{AlScN}$) grown on a Silicon Carbide ($	ext{SiC}$) substrate. The coupling mechanism relies on the piezoelectric effect to mediate interaction between microwave photons and acoustic phonons.
key_observables: Superconducting resonator coherent lifetime ($2.9 \mu	ext{s}$), low phononic propagation loss at $4.05 	ext{ GHz}$, estimated phonon lifetime ($7.6 \mu	ext{s}$), and electromechanical coupling coefficient ($\approx 4.3\%$).
important_parameters: Operating frequency around $4.175 	ext{ GHz}$; coherence times in the microsecond regime; theoretical upper bound for $ eta$ of $8\%$.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that selective etching and material deposition can create a stable, low-loss interface supporting both superconducting metal films and piezoelectric phononic layers simultaneously.
figures_summary: Figure 5 conceptually illustrates the potential application of this platform for quantum acoustic circuits, such as Gaussian boson sampling, within the AlScN-on-SiC structure.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for a monolithic coupling platform, details the proposed $	ext{Al}$-on-$	ext{SiC}/	ext{AlScN}$-on-$	ext{SiC}$ architecture via selective etching, and presents characterization results showing compatible lifetimes and measurable electromechanical coupling.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the integration challenge in quantum hardware by proposing a material system ($	ext{AlScN/SiC}$) that allows for coexisting superconducting and phononic elements on one chip, which is crucial for realizing scalable hybrid quantum processors.
